results.evidence: The AAJ report (published 2016) dates the climb July 6, 2015; the Alpinist newswire piece and the first-ascent trip report titled 7/6/2015 agree. This row's fa, overview and beta all said 2004 and are corrected; the sister Southeast Route row already says 2015.
This row's overview (2015) is correct per the AAJ report, Alpinist and the FA trip report (July 6, 2015); the sister Stonehenge row was wrong and is fixed in its own result.

The 1961 first-ascent account (AAJ 1962) describes a class IV line following a ledge onto the north face from the west notch; Wikipedia lists the easiest route only as class 5, and the row's own corrections note cites an 'awkward 5.7 step-around'. No source names a 'Southeast Route' or gives Grade IV 5.8, but a replacement grade (and the commitment/alpine grade to match) is not settled by two sources.

results.fact: Aspect / side of the peak climbed
results.evidence: The FA account climbs from the west (Himmel-Otto) notch via a ledge onto the north face, supporting the NW fields; but no source describes a route called 'Southeast Route', so it is unclear whether the row's name or its prose is the error. One source only; left open.

The published Crescent Creek approach and the FA account mention no glacier on the route, but the lower Barrier crossing runs at the toe of the Terror Glacier, and no source states whether parties rope up for glacier travel. Not settled by two sources.

No external source gives a rappel count or a false-summit-notch descent for this line (that false-summit notch belongs to Wild Hair Crack's description). The descent is undocumented beyond reversing the route.

Four fields end the season in September, but an ascent of Wild Hair Crack from the same col is documented on Oct 4, 2020, so an external record supports October climbing against the internal majority. Not settled.
